The November 1, 2017 FOMC statement conveys a growth-positive but inflation-cautious tone: labor markets are strengthening and activity is “solid,” yet both headline and core inflation are below 2 percent. In line with New Keynesian policy guidance (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), the Committee appropriately looks through hurricane-driven, energy-related price spikes and maintains an accommodative stance while expectations appear anchored. The emphasis on “gradual” rate increases and a path for the funds rate below its longer-run level reflects rule-like behavior and interest-rate smoothing consistent with the Taylor (1993) framework, while the continuation of balance-sheet normalization fits post-crisis operating insights discussed by Goodfriend (2002) and the Fed’s broader toolkit of QE and forward guidance. Net: solid real-side momentum with balanced risks, tempered by soft inflation—yielding a modestly positive overall tone.
